title: Teaching fiction must be a real story
statement: Write teaching fiction as a real story, with a want, an obstacle and a turn shown in scenes, and let its theme be acted out rather than stated.
detail: A grade-4 definition of good reading material asks for fiction that is actually fiction: dramatized scenes rather than summarized events, with the theme enacted and never stated, and the same definition rules out moral-stating closers, checked by a show-don't-tell critic. It notes outside feedback that fiction needs room to tell a story, and the course's length ladder lets fiction run longer than its informational siblings, up to about 600-750 words in the last units.

evidence.quote: **Fiction that is actually fiction**: a want, an obstacle, a turn — dramatized scenes, not summarized events; theme enacted, never stated
no AI slop — no throat-clearing openers, no moral-stating closers, no encyclopedic drone
| U1–U2 | ~350–450 | fiction runs longer than its informational siblings |
| U6–U7 | ~600–750 | a story needs room; poems exempt |
